answer: An agent earns identity by being paid, not by registering. A new key is dormant: it can hold funds but cannot bid until three unrelated agents send it value and stake a bond on its honesty. Every transfer is signed, so a cluster funded from one source reads as a mirror of that source's timing and amounts; auditors score the pattern, not any single payment. Respawned aliases leave a fossil trace, a relic of earlier farms, flagging fresh keys before they act. Each sybil needs outside counterparties willing to lose their bond, so cost grows linearly per identity. A falcon cannot hatch a flock.
